title: WRitEer: A Multi-Objective, Preference-Driven Multi-Agent Framework for Human-Like Advanced Text Generation
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

publication.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence

parentSelection: Fitness-based prompt crossover with local dimension mutation

mechanism.domainTask: Human-like advanced text generation with evolutionary prompt optimization and preference fine-tuning
mechanism.populationDetail: The Editor initializes five prompt combinations and evolves a current prompt through a three-round sequence; no island or tree structure is described.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is described; the method selects the highest-fitness prompt from its current population.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The paper specifies best-individual selection and sequential operators but does not state a population-wide survivor replacement policy.
mechanism.generationDetail: Crossover fuses prompt dimensions from the current candidate and a highest-fitness population member; mutation locally regenerates only subprompts for the worst dynamic-metric dimensions.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Static/dynamic metrics drive prompt fitness and output choice; chosen/rejected output pairs are accumulated for periodic DPO updates.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Crossover combines the current prompt with the highest-fitness population member (two parents); mutation edits only the current prompt. Selection is not a uniform parent rule across operators.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Preference triples from evaluated text pairs periodically fine-tune the Writer with DPO, coupling test-time evolutionary prompt search with online model adaptation.
